facility_name: Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), Ikeja - new Dialysis Unit
evidence_note: LASUTH opened a new dialysis unit with 8 stations, run as a private-public venture. No private partner is named. "The unit has eight dialysis stations capable of a minimum of 22 sessions daily and 660 sessions monthly."

facility_name: Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), Ikeja - Critical Care Unit
evidence_note: Six dialysis machines already in the CCU, separate from the 8 new stations. The same article also mentions 2 dedicated machines for HIV/hepatitis patients. "the existing six dialysis machines in the Critical Care Unit (CCU) of the hospital"

facility_name: Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), Ikeja
evidence_note: Later report: 7 working machines (5 + 2). This conflicts with the 2022 figure of 8 stations + 6 CCU machines. Session cost N40,000. "there were five working dialysis machines at the Special Services Centre, and two at the Dialysis Centre."

facility_name: Gbagada General Hospital
evidence_note: The medical director says six machines are working. Session cost N43,000. "six machines were working in the dialysis centre."

facility_name: Alimosho General Hospital, Igando
evidence_note: Three working machines. Unreliable electricity limits the unit to one batch of dialysis a day. Session cost N45,000 plus consumables. "due to the situation with electricity, could only run a batch of dialysis per day"
State-wide count of working dialysis machines in Lagos State government facilities, LASUTH included. "In all, the state can only boast of 18 working dialysis in its facilities."
Only 3 of 28 Lagos State general hospitals have dialysis (General Hospital Lagos, Gbagada, Alimosho). "only three out of 28 general hospitals in the state operate with dialysis machines."

facility_name: Randle General Hospital; Isolo General Hospital; General Hospital Ikorodu
evidence_note: These three large state general hospitals have no dialysis machines or renal centre. "Randle General Hospital, Isolo General Hospital and General Hospital, Ikorodu have no dialysis machines"

facility_name: Lagos State Cardiac and Renal Centre, Gbagada
evidence_note: 24 machines at commissioning in 2015. The centre is now abandoned. A nephrologist doubts any machine still works and blames salt deposits blocking machine valves. "I'll be surprised if any of them are still working"

facility_name: Lagos State Cardiac and Renal Centre, Gbagada
evidence_note: Lagos Assembly committee: the centre's machines ran for two weeks before it was locked up. The cause is under probe and not stated. "the cardio renal machines only worked for two weeks before the facility was locked up."

facility_name: Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), Idi-Araba - Lion Isaac Olusola Dada Dialysis Centre
evidence_note: New centre (32 beds) handed to LUTH. It replaces a 40-year-old unit described as 'grossly inadequate and dilapidated'. Full operation was still pending. "32 beds would be added to the 150 beds in the entire dialysis centres in Lagos."

facility_name: Federal Medical Centre, Ebute Metta
evidence_note: Listed among 11 federal hospitals in the federal dialysis subsidy (N12,000 per session). No machine count is given. Named in list as: "Federal Medical Centre, Ebute Metta, Lagos"

facility_name: Olabisi Onabanjo University Teaching Hospital (OOUTH), Sagamu - Enoch and Folu Adeboye Dialysis Centre
evidence_note: RCCG/His Love Foundation donated a dialysis centre with 3 machines, a water RO system and a 30kVA generator. "three dialysis machines" ... "one medical water reserve osmosis purification system"

facility_name: Federal Medical Centre, Idi-Aba, Abeokuta
evidence_note: Two machines (N20m) bought for COVID-19 and viral-disease patients, who had previously been referred elsewhere. Says nothing on any other machines. "two brand new dialysis machines" ... "solely dedicated to covid-19 and other viral related diseases"

facility_name: University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan
evidence_note: The CMD reports 3 haemodialysis machines bought for N30m and working. "we acquired three hemodialysis machines amounting to N30 million which were functioning well"

facility_name: University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan
evidence_note: A solar system was installed for the haemodialysis centre. The consultant nephrologist (Dr Sam Ajayi) says power was the missing piece. "the systems cannot run efficiently without adequate power."

facility_name: University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan
evidence_note: At least one consultant nephrologist is named at UCH. This is a minimum, not a total. Sam Ajayi is described as "consultant nephrologist at UCH Ibadan"

facility_name: University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan
evidence_note: Listed among 11 federal hospitals in the N12,000-per-session federal dialysis subsidy. Named in list as: "University College Hospital, Ibadan"

facility_name: LAUTECH Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso
evidence_note: Eight haemodialysis machines acquired. This is an old source (2013) and current status is unknown. "has acquired eight Haemo dialysis machines to boost its infrastructural facilities"

facility_name: Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospitals Complex (OAUTHC), Ile-Ife
evidence_note: The renal replacement programme was 'reactivated' (reason not stated) and the old renal unit renovated. 15 donated machines. Total fleet and working status are not given. "friends of the hospital in Canada and the United States had donated 15 additional dialysis machines"

facility_name: Wesley Guild Hospital, Ilesa (OAUTHC)
evidence_note: RCCG donated a dialysis centre with 3 machines, a water RO system and a 30kVA generator. "three dialysis machines" ... "one water reverse osmosis purification system"

facility_name: State General Hospital, Osogbo (and Osun State general hospitals)
evidence_note: A doctor at General Hospital Osogbo said the state general hospitals had no dialysis machines. "the state general hospitals had no dialysis machines for kidney disease treatment"

facility_name: Ekiti State University Teaching Hospital (EKSUTH), Ado-Ekiti - Enoch and Folu Adeboye Dialysis Centre
evidence_note: Centre commissioned with 3 new machines, a water treatment unit and a 50kVA generator. Before this, the hospital averaged 40 dialysis sessions a month. "three brand new dialysis machines" ... "the hospital averaged 40 dialysis per month"

facility_name: Ekiti State University Teaching Hospital (EKSUTH), Ado-Ekiti
evidence_note: Hospital official reports existing machines working (pre-2025 centre). No count given. "the dialysis machines in the facility were working well and serving patients"

facility_name: Federal Teaching Hospital, Ado-Ekiti (as written in source; CMD Prof. Adekunle Ajayi - likely Federal Teaching Hospital Ido-Ekiti, verify)
evidence_note: The CMD reported 6 machines in use for kidney patients. The facility naming in the source is ambiguous. "the facility had six dialysis machines serving kidney patients from the state"

facility_name: Kidney Care Centre, Medical Village, Ondo town
evidence_note: State-established kidney centre with 15 installed machines and subsidised fees. Weak source: a 2013 blog repost of a Sunday Vanguard story (original blocked). "15 kidney dialysis machines have been installed in the centre located at the Medical Village in Ondo town."

facility_name: University of Medical Sciences Teaching Hospital (UNIMEDTH), Akure
evidence_note: In 2019 a dialysis centre was planned (Lions Club MoU, N50m), suggesting none was in place at the Akure complex. "would reduce the rate of death associated with the movement of kidney patients from one hospital to another"

facility_name: University of Medical Sciences Teaching Hospital, Ondo (Akindayomi-Adeboye Intensive Care Centre)
evidence_note: Listed in a 2022 RCCG foundation record of dialysis centres. The April 2021 centre included a dialysis unit. No machine count. "incorporated an ICU, kidney dialysis unit, cardiac diagnostic unit, and X-ray unit."
